claims.text: Compiler-precise, cross-file symbol resolution is SCIP / tree-sitter-stack-graphs territory: months of per-language work.
claims.why: Claims about SCIP and stack-graphs are not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: This is the honest v1 — a NAME-based reference graph over the units the parser already extracted: for a unit, which *other known unit names* appear as identifier tokens in its body.
claims.why: The code indeed uses identifier token matching (identifiers function) and name-based lookups (callees, callers).

claims.text: Movement I.5 / Move 4 sharpens it with import/scope awareness.
claims.why: Referenced movements not in this chunk.

claims.text: Given a SymbolResolver (a per-file symbol table + the Move-2 import edges), resolution instead prefers, in order: 1. a unit defined in the SAME file as the reference, 2. a unit in a module the file actually IMPORTS, 3. the global-name fallback (the old behavior) only when 1+2 find nothing.
claims.why: SymbolResolver.resolve implements exactly this order: same-file defs first, then imported defs, returns None otherwise.

claims.text: This drops false call edges -> tighter distill slices + a truer call graph.
claims.why: Effect on distill slices cannot be verified from this code.

claims.text: Python is precise (its import graph is precise); other languages are best-effort (their import resolution is best-effort).
claims.why: No import graph construction code in this chunk.

claims.text: Full scope/shadowing is deliberately NOT attempted here — that is SCIP / stack-graphs, deferred, not faked.
claims.why: The code does not implement scope/shadowing; SymbolResolver.resolve uses simple name-based lookup.

claims.text: Backward-compatible: callees/callers take an OPTIONAL resolver that defaults to None (the pure name-match), so existing callers (slice.py) are unaffected.
claims.why: Both callees and callers have resolver parameter defaulting to None, and branch accordingly.

claims.text: SORTED TUPLES, not sets. ... Normalising HERE rather than in build_resolver means every construction path is deterministic, including hand-built resolvers.
claims.why: The code sorts the values in imports_by_file and reassigns the attribute.

claims.text: Same candidates, now a total order; ties break on rel path.
claims.why: Sorting the tuple of strings gives a total order; ties are identical strings thus irrelevant.

claims.text: SORTED, not raw set order. ... Same hits, now a total order.
claims.why: The loop iterates over sorted(used), ensuring deterministic order.

claims.text: A leaf that 5000 modules transitively depend on is either a pathological graph or a blast radius so large that escalating is right anyway, so the cap is not a correctness compromise -- but the caller MUST treat truncated as 'could not prove safe', never as 'safe'.
claims.why: The actual usage of REACH_VISIT_CAP in fenced_reachability is not fully visible.

claims.text: Path normalised for fence matching: forward slashes, lower-cased, and ROOT-ANCHORED with a leading '/'.
claims.why: The function replaces backslashes, lowercases, and prepends '/' after stripping leading slashes.

claims.text: The leading slash is deliberate and is NOT what sensitivity._norm does.
claims.why: sensitivity._norm is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The generic fence ships fragments like /controller and /safety, which a repo-relative rel (controller/hv_interlock.py) cannot contain -- so anchoring here catches top-level fenced trees that a bare substring test misses.
claims.why: Behavior of 'bare substring test' not verifiable; but the logic of prepending '/' is confirmed.

claims.text: It can only ever match MORE than the literal check, which is the direction this whole module is allowed to err in.
claims.why: Cannot compare to 'literal check' not present.

claims.text: The first fenced fragment matching rel, or None. Fragment order comes from the policy tuple (a total order), so the reported reason is stable.

claims.text: Spelling is a BYPASS CLASS, not a cosmetic detail: the fence is keyed on graph membership, so Utils/Clamp.py (Windows hands back either case), ./utils/clamp.py and utils/../utils/clamp.py all used to miss the node and read as 'no known dependents' -- i.e. as safe. Resolve the spelling before deciding, never after.
claims.why: The function normalizes the rel path and tries exact match, then case-insensitive match.

claims.text: Nodes of the DEPENDENCY graph. Code only.
claims.why: The function collects from code_modules and import edges, not documents.

claims.text: Documents are excluded deliberately, and this is a safety decision rather than a tidiness one. ... A document has no import edges by construction, so every one of them would land in the denominator and none in the numerator: turning documents on would DILUTE the fence's dominance fraction with files that cannot reach anything, making a guardrail less likely to fire for a bookkeeping reason.
claims.why: Dominance fraction and guardrail behavior not in this chunk.
